what: how big a compiled program is, per part - the input the image format is designed against
findings: AN IMAGE IS NOT AUTOMATICALLY SMALLER THAN THE SOURCE IT REPLACES. p5 is 66% and phaser 44%, but BABYLON IS 139% - 15.7 MB of image for 11.3 MB of source, because 31,905 protos carry 9.98 MB of 8-byte instructions. Anyone assuming an image shrinks the application is wrong on the largest corpus.

AND program::source IS RETAINED ON TOP OF THAT, because f.toString() has to hand back text and p5's own error system reads its source. Keeping it makes babylon 27 MB - 2.4x the source. Whether the image keeps it, drops it, or makes it optional is the format's biggest size lever.

THE PER-PROTO NAME TABLES ARE 80-83% DUPLICATE and pooling them across the image is a large, cheap win: babylon's 166,396 name entries are 24,172 unique, 2686 KB -> 495 KB. Phaser 553 -> 96 KB, p5 333 -> 68 KB. This is a v1 decision rather than a later optimisation, because it changes the format.
STRING LITERALS ARE NOT DUPLICATE in the same way - babylon 2050 KB -> 1840 KB - so pooling them buys little and the effort belongs on names.
